sidecar_purpose: Repo-resident semantic image sidecar for the Bit and Bot hero source image in the bit-and-bot asset pack. Supports hero selection, visual continuity, prompt constraint extraction, and QA for the bit-bot robot duo.
source_truth_note: This sidecar is derived visual evidence for the referenced image. The repo image bytes and package manifest remain authoritative for custody; this sidecar does not authorize derivative images or broaden canon.
runtime_use_note: Use this sidecar for textual hero selection, continuity checks, and prompt planning. Inspect the image pixels directly when exact composition, expression, prop placement, or fine visual details matter.
do_not_infer_note: Do not infer unseen alternate views, additional expressions, extra props, story state, or acceptance of derivative images beyond the observed hero pose and stated intended use.

provenance.prompt_unretained_note: Provenance has not been determined for this image.

summary: Bit and Bot hero source image: an isolated full-body hero pose of the red-and-blue wheeled robot duo on a clean white or very light background. Bit, the smaller red-coded robot, appears alongside Bot, the taller blue-coded robot, in a friendly paired composition. Both retain the bit-bot visual canon: rounded white shells, glossy black face screens, colored digital marks, and two-wheel lower bodies. The image serves as the canonical hero source for the bit-and-bot duo, pending pixel-level review.

composition: Portrait-oriented source render of Bit and Bot centered in the frame, isolated on a clean white or very light background with ample padding.
Two-figure hero composition showing the paired red-coded and blue-coded robots.
Full-body or near-full-body framing suitable as a canonical duo reference.
No detailed environment or scene background; the characters are the sole subjects.
character: Bit is the smaller, faster red-coded wheeled robot of the bit-and-bot duo.
Bot is the taller, steadier blue-coded wheeled robot of the bit-and-bot duo.
Both have rounded white body shells with black internal mechanical structure.
Glossy black face screens with colored digital marks for eyes and mouth.
Bit's accent color is red; Bot's accent color is blue.
Single antenna on each robot, with Bit's tip in red and Bot's in blue.
Rounded, friendly toy-like proportions and approachable expressions.
costume_and_form: Two-wheel lower body for each robot, forming the bit-bot mobile base.
Red circular joints at ears, shoulders, wrists, torso plate, and wheel hubs on Bit.
Blue circular joints and trim corresponding to Bot's color code.
Race bibs may be present on one or both robots; exact bib text should be verified against pixels.
colors: Dominant white shell for both robots.
Black mechanical structure and glossy face screens.
Isolated white or near-white background with soft pale grey ground shadow.
style: Clean editorial illustration with rounded linework.
role_cues: The paired red-coded and blue-coded wheeled robots identify the characters as Bit and Bot.
The two-wheel base and rounded robot shells distinguish the bit-bot duo from humanoid or drone designs.
The clean, isolated, full-figure presentation marks the image as a source hero asset.

positive_constraints: Preserve Bit as the smaller red-coded wheeled robot and Bot as the taller blue-coded wheeled robot.
Keep both robots' rounded white shells, black mechanical structure, and glossy black face screens.
Maintain the red accent system for Bit and the blue accent system for Bot.
Preserve the two-wheel lower body and toy-like proportions for both characters.
Keep the isolated white background and soft pale grey ground shadow where present.
Use this image as the canonical hero source for bit-and-bot duo continuity and prompt variation.
negative_constraints: Do not swap the color codes: Bit must stay red and Bot must stay blue.
Do not redesign either robot as a sleek drone, humanoid android, or menacing machine.
Do not remove the wheels or change the two-wheel lower body on either character.
Do not add busy backgrounds, non-bit-bot accessories, or extra props not in the image.
Do not infer additional expressions, poses, or final acceptance beyond the observed hero view.

best_for: Selecting the canonical Bit and Bot hero pose for scene assembly in the bit-bot set.
Hero continuity and prompt variation for bit-and-bot duo compositions.
Reference for Bit and Bot's color system, silhouette, and paired presentation.
QA that generated bit-and-bot art remains on-model and on-palette.
not_sufficient_for: Final character turnaround or full expression reference for either robot.
Final asset acceptance without pixel-level QA against the source image.
Authorizing derivative images or unobserved alternate poses.
Detailed prop or environment canon beyond the visible hero frame.
